analysis: What changed versus the 4:00 AM brief: the rotation hardened rather than faded. Dow futures improved to +0.68% and S&P futures ticked up to +0.13%, while Nasdaq-100 futures stayed down ~0.6% — the same split, now with premarket megacap prices to back it: Amazon +1.83% and Meta +1.04% while Nvidia slipped further to -1.80% and the whole chip complex (AMD, Micron, Marvell -2.3% each, SOXL -6.3%) kept selling. The fresh macro item is the Bank of England hiking to 4%, its first rise since August 2023, with an 8-1 vote and a warning that more hikes follow if the US-Iran conflict continues — a reminder that the inflation/energy channel behind Wednesday's oil crash is still live, even as the 10-year slipped to ~4.85% and gold pushed to $4,144. Two counterweights to the data-center-slowdown story landed: Google's $15B Malaysia data-center investment for 2027-28 and Meta's heavily oversubscribed $15B bond raise plus an inaugural euro bond — hyperscalers are still spending, just more selectively. Tesla deepened its political slide (-2.14% premarket). Signal vs noise: the Dow/S&P-vs-Nasdaq split, the chip margin squeeze, the BoE hike and the hyperscaler spending are signal; premarket quote wiggles and single-name earnings reactions are noise. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads surfaced — HN results were stale or unrelated and the Reddit search returned nothing — so community_signals is empty rather than padded.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures are still split an hour later: as of about 6:28 a.m. ET, Dow futures were up 0.68% (+364 pts), S&P 500 futures up 0.13% and Nasdaq-100 futures down 0.59% (-169 pts), after Wednesday's rally (Dow +3.03% to 53,356.12, S&P +1.58% to 7,688.62, Nasdaq +1.44% to 25,736.51).
headlines.why_it_matters: The rotation is holding, not fading — Dow futures actually improved from +0.48% at the 4 a.m. read while the Nasdaq stayed down, so breadth is still carrying the tape while tech drags.

headlines.headline: The Bank of England raised rates for the first time in over three years, hiking 25bp to 4% from 3.75% on an 8-1 vote (Catherine Mann dissented, wanting 4.25%), and warned at least one more increase is likely if the US-Iran conflict continues; UK CPI was 3.5% in September and is expected to reach around 5% by mid-2027. Sterling edged up to about $1.3477 and gilt yields rose.
headlines.why_it_matters: A major central bank hiking while the Fed is priced for a December hike keeps the global rate backdrop tight — and it ties directly to the energy/inflation channel that drove Wednesday's 8% oil crash.

headlines.headline: Nvidia fell 1.80% in premarket trading to $196.53, deeper than the -0.4% seen at the 4 a.m. read, as the chip selloff spread: AMD, Micron and Marvell were each down about 2.3%, Broadcom -1.3%, the SOX-style ETF SMH -2.0% and leveraged SOXL -6.3%, while Qualcomm held around -10% after its handset miss and margin-guide cut.
headlines.why_it_matters: The chip leg is not stabilizing into the open — the memory-cost squeeze that hit Qualcomm is now repricing the whole semi complex, and Nvidia is the tape's biggest weight in that move.

headlines.headline: The hyperscalers kept their bid in premarket trading: Amazon +1.83% to $270.89, Meta +1.04% to $636.53, Alphabet +0.81% to $291.27, Apple +0.76% to $352.15 and Microsoft +0.24% to $557.16, all as of about 7:53 a.m. ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: Scarce compute is still being read as a tailwind for the incumbents that already own it — the megacaps are absorbing the bid the chips are losing, which is what keeps the S&P future flat instead of down.

headlines.headline: Tesla fell 2.14% in premarket trading to $376.96, extending Wednesday's losses and the slide in SpaceX on continued scrutiny of a prospective merger and of Musk's Texas footprint after Democratic wins in Texas and the Senate.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla keeps trading on Washington headlines rather than operations — the political discount persists until the new Congress is seated Jan 3.

headlines.headline: Qualcomm held around -10% in premarket trading after fiscal Q4 handset revenue fell 26% to $5.14 billion and chip-design margins were guided down to 20-22% from 24% on rising memory and input costs, despite revenue of $10.4 billion beating the $10.1 billion expected; Q1 guidance of $10.4-11.2 billion also disappointed.
headlines.why_it_matters: The memory shortage is a margin story now, not just a supply story — Qualcomm's guide cut shows handset weakness plus cost inflation hitting the same quarter, and it is dragging the whole chip tape with it.

headlines.headline: After the close today: Airbnb (EPS est. $2.85, revenue est. $4.75B), DraftKings, IonQ (revenue est. ~$141M, loss ~$0.79/share) and SoundHound AI (revenue est. ~$61.7M, +47% year over year) all report Q3 results, along with IREN. SoundHound reports after a Q2 beat that lifted its 2026 revenue guide to $230-260M; IonQ was down 2.37% premarket ahead of its print.
headlines.why_it_matters: A crowded after-close slate in AI-adjacent names (quantum, voice AI, data-center hosting) lands right as the AI-infrastructure trade is being repriced — these prints will either steady the tape or extend the split.

headlines.headline: Alphabet's Google plans to invest $15 billion in Malaysia between 2027 and 2028 to build new data-center campuses and expand cloud capacity, while Meta completed a $15 billion U.S. dollar bond offering on Nov 3 that drew about $58 billion in orders (3.9x oversubscribed) and launched its inaugural euro bond sale on Nov 4 targeting $5-10 billion.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hyperscalers are still spending big on AI infrastructure even as the buildout outlook slows — the slowdown story is about the marginal builders, not the incumbents, which is why their stocks keep rising.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight; the Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. The $0.525 distribution pays tomorrow, Friday Nov 6. On the earnings call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.

watch_next: 8:30 a.m. ET today: weekly initial jobless claims (about 197,000 expected vs 194,000 prior), plus Fed speakers including Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin.
Friday Nov 6: October nonfarm payrolls (consensus about 55,000 jobs, unemployment expected to hold at 4.2%); USAC's $0.525 distribution pays.
Whether the Nasdaq-100's chip-led drag spreads to the broader tape or the Dow/S&P rotation keeps the rally intact into the open.
After the close today: Airbnb, DraftKings, IonQ, SoundHound AI and IREN report Q3 results.
